enumeration.method: Enumerate printed uppercase Theorem environments independently on PDF pages 1-25 and compare their source order with the saved inventory. Visually review full statements on pages 3, 10-16 and 18; include Theorem 4 continuation on page 12. Main references end on page 25 and the supplement title starts page 26.

checks: All eleven original theorem records remain identical to the independently validated source inventory. The final census pins the unchanged inventory SHA-256.

Pinned source identity, title, authors, arXiv stamp, PDF page count and SHA-256 were checked. Main-text heading enumeration yields exactly Theorems 1-11; Lemma 1 and Proposition 1 are excluded from the theorem inventory.

All 37 local source passages and 14 auxiliary passages were reviewed against main-text pages. The source algorithms retain outer cross-fitting, inner split/swap where present, both treatment paths and the variance outputs.
The independent validator accepts the final census, local DAG, derived metrics, source identity, keyword names, selectors and source-backed explanations for all 158 related-theorem connections.

Algorithm 1 reaches only Theorems 2-3; Algorithm 2 reaches only Theorems 4-5. The averaged DR component fit additionally reaches Theorem 9, and the nested component fit additionally reaches Theorem 10.

General DR Theorems 6-7 do not acquire logistic/Lasso population projections or the sub-Gaussian Assumptions 2-3. Assumption 5 imports the residual definitions with general working models, not the full parametric tail hypothesis.
Theorem 8 depends only on its separate generic imputed-Lasso setup and the shared Orlicz norm. Theorem 11 depends only on its multi-stage model, nuisance definitions and Assumption 6.

Theorems 4-5 retain the explicit nested-model replacement in Assumption 2 via separate local application records. Theorem 10 lacks that instruction, so its literal reference and resulting ambiguity remain visible.

Theorem 2 retains s2 versus s2-prime and the NR indicator. Theorems 9-10 retain the signed r-th powers, and the parametric score retains its delta_c subscript. Magnified source crops corroborate these details.
Theorem 10 imports the rate expression of Theorem 9(c), without importing the correctness condition, Assumption 4 or the DR component-fit algorithm.

Every interface has a natural-language source keyword and a meaning-bearing source selector, plus an explanation following its exact same-paper dependency path. All transcribed mathematical fragments have balanced braces.

source_notes: The audit is source-specific to the May 2023 preprint associated with the 2024 corpus entry. Journal-version equality has not been assumed.
Theorem 4 spans two pages; its complete s1-prime and s2-prime definitions were checked. Theorem 8 preserves both finite-probability and asymptotic bounds. Theorem 9 preserves all three rate branches.
Displayed source discrepancies are archived separately without repairing the original statements. They are limitations for later formalization, not evidence that the paper census is incomplete.
The introductory supplement text exposed by an earlier boundary crop is not used or retained as statement evidence. Only the supplement title crop documents that boundary.

evidence.location: Theorem 2 — displayed rate and final definitions

unresolved_source_references.detail: The rate prints s2, but the subsequent definition names s2-prime. That definition also uses the indicator mu_a,NR-star != mu_a despite the S-DRL setting. Both are retained; there is a literal local dependency on the nested target and no silent s2 or model-symbol repair.

The argument eta binds delta without a path subscript, but the final denominator prints delta_c. A path-specific interpretation is plausible, but no substitution is made in the original score formula.

Both theorems print {E[mu-hat-mu-star]^r}^{1/r} without absolute-value bars, for any constant r>=1. For noninteger r and signed errors this lacks an ordinary real-valued interpretation. Neither expression is rewritten as an absolute moment or Lr norm.

Theorem 10 cites Assumptions 1-3 without the explicit replacement of mu-star and beta-star by their NR counterparts used in Theorems 4-5. Its literal reference to Assumption 2 is preserved. Whether a nested-model substitution was intended remains unresolved; the resulting DR-target dependence is not concealed.

The reference to r_n in Theorem 9(c) resolves only the expression used in the bound. Theorem 10 does not explicitly assume nu-star=nu, Assumption 4 or the DR inner-split fitting method; these are not imported through the reference.

The procedures loop over both a and a-prime, and residuals/score contrasts include both paths. Many displayed regularity and sparsity conditions are written only with subscript a, without an explicit max over the two paths. The audit preserves that wording; it does not add an unstated uniform quantifier or maximum to the original theorem.

Theorem 2 through Theorem 5 do not print explicit tuning-rate choices for the four penalties. Their algorithms refer to objectives with positive penalties; Theorems 9-10 separately state tuning rates for the nuisance fits. The latter rates are not retroactively inserted into earlier theorem statements.

Equal K-fold sizes and, in Algorithm 1, equal inner halves require divisibility. Section 2.4 explicitly treats n=N/K as an integer; Algorithm 1 does not supply a rounding convention. K>=2 is printed but no growth regime for K is specified in the inventoried limit statements.

The score scale can shrink to zero asymptotically. Exact positivity of sigma is not explicitly asserted in Assumption 2, although reciprocal normalizations and rates divided by sigma require it; Assumption 5 also has ratios with residual second moments in denominators. No zero-denominator convention is supplied or invented.

The source defines the squared score contrast centered at the true theta. Under arbitrary misspecification this need not be the variance centered at its own expectation. The squared-moment definition is retained even where the source uses variance terminology.

The terminal working mean is defined as mu-star_(T+1)(s-bar_(T+1),a-bar_T):=s_(T+1). No separate scalar coordinate s_(T+1) is defined beforehand, while the next sentence explicitly identifies the terminal working and true means with Y under consistency. Both sentences are retained; the last-outcome-coordinate interpretation is recorded, not substituted into the original.

The overlap probability contains lower-case s-bar_t rather than random S-bar_t. This differs from Assumption 1(c), which uses random covariates. The source argument is preserved without changing the scope to a pointwise or almost-sure condition.

Theorem 11 states t<=T-1 without a lower bound. The following discussion explicitly includes t=0; the stage-zero empty-history convention supports that case. Negative times are not defined and are not added as meaningful inputs.

The source writes argmin objects without a universal tie-breaking or existence convention for every input. Conditional expectations evaluated at specified covariates require versions, with no all-point version selection specified. These are recorded formalization prerequisites, not repaired definitions.

The theorem defines epsilon_i and then bounds the unindexed epsilon Orlicz norm. The natural independent-copy residual Y-star-X-transpose beta-star is supported by the pre-theorem independent-copy setup, but is not explicitly defined in the theorem body.

The gauge formula is stated for x>0, whereas the norm evaluates it at |X|/c, possibly zero. Extending exp(x^alpha)-1 to zero is conventional, but the printed domain restriction is not silently rewritten.

ambient_resolution.shared: D1 and A2 resolve S1,S2,S,d1,d2,d and two-stage observations; D8 resolves W_i,N and training subsets. A3-A4 and equations (2.1)-(2.2) resolve augmented vectors u,v,U,V. Norm subscripts 0,1,2,infinity are support count, l1, Euclidean and supremum vector norms; matrix lambda_min is the minimum eigenvalue. E/P, conditional independence, indicator functions, finite products, Gaussian N(0,1), argmin and stochastic order have ordinary meanings subject to the source issues below. No library availability is asserted.
ambient_resolution.1: D3 supplies true and working conditional functions and D5 the causal conditions; s1 is universally quantified inside the theorem. The working-function equality is the correctness premise, not a linear/logistic restriction. Positivity/integrability conventions beyond those printed are not inserted.
ambient_resolution.2: D19 is Algorithm 1; D2 is theta; D22 is sigma. A6 resolves four sparsities to D9/D10/D12. C and the bounded/unbounded alternatives are inline. s1 and s2-prime are defined inline; s2 remains the source discrepancy. The NR-model indicator is connected literally to D13. Assumptions 1-4 stay separate.
ambient_resolution.3: The same S-DRL targets and sparsities as Theorem 2; Algorithm 1 provides both estimated theta and sigma. The extra two product-sparsity terms are inline, and Assumption 4 is not explicitly assumed or imported through estimator definitions.
ambient_resolution.4: D20 is Algorithm 2; D13 and A7 resolve the nested beta sparsity. D23NR and D22NR preserve the explicit nested-model application of Assumption 2 and sigma. s1-prime and s2-prime are defined in the continuation on page 12. No inner DR split is imported.
ambient_resolution.5: D20 supplies the nested estimator and fitted variance; D22NR is the explicitly substituted population scale. The three product-sparsity terms are inline; Assumption 4 is not added.
ambient_resolution.6: D26 is the general cross-fitted estimator, D27 its population score scale, and D30 the rate/moment assumption. A9 resolves fresh-covariate expectations. q_N and C_mu are local binders. Correctness alternatives refer to general functions, not the parametric projections.
ambient_resolution.7: D26/D27 supply the two variance normalizations and D30 the rates. The two product requirements are inline; d may remain fixed as expressly stated. Referencing residual definitions in Assumption 5 does not import the sub-Gaussian Assumption 2.
ambient_resolution.8: D31 supplies the generic M-sample regression experiment, beta-star and beta-hat. The source defines s, epsilon_i, E1, delta_M, lambda_M and the constants inside the theorem; D6 resolves psi2. The unindexed residual epsilon uses the independent-copy convention, recorded as a source notation issue. A14 confirms imputed responses need not be mutually independent or independent of covariates. No causal assumptions apply.
ambient_resolution.9: D16 plus its archived Step 9 averaging instruction and A10 resolve beta-hat_a and mu-hat_a. D12 supplies the population target; A6 resolves sparsities; D9/D10 supply second-stage working targets in the three branches. r,lambda_alpha,lambda_beta,lambda_delta,C and r_n are inline. The signed prediction-moment expression is retained. No full DTE contrast algorithm is needed to define the fitted first-time mean.
ambient_resolution.10: D17/A11 resolve the nested fit and conditional mean; D13/A7 resolve the nested target and sparsity. A12 resolves only the rate expression referenced from Theorem 9(c). The literal Assumption 2 reference yields D23/D22 rather than an invented NR substitution; this ambiguity is recorded explicitly. No nu-star=nu hypothesis is imported from the referenced rate branch.
ambient_resolution.11: D32 resolves W_T,bar-S_t,bar-A_t,bar-a_t,T and dimensions; D33 and A13 resolve the nuisance functions and initial/terminal conditions. D34 is Assumption 6. The score psi-star is defined inline with products over subsequent stages; t=0 is supported by the following paragraph and empty histories. The theorem is independent of logistic/Lasso models. Proposition 1 is a separate non-Theorem result and is not a prerequisite.
